chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect at rs13078086
predictions: The T and G alleles will not show a reproducible TF-dependent regulatory difference at this site; any association with colorectal cancer could instead reflect linkage or no causal effect.
falsified_if: In an appropriate regulatory assay, the alleles show a reproducible difference in TF-dependent activity that is attributable to this sequence.

chains.title: Speculative TCF7L2-dependent activation
chains.element: A putative cis-regulatory element overlapping rs13078086; its regulatory activity is unestablished.

links.claim: Hypothesis: the G (alt) allele binds TCF7L2 more strongly than the T (ref) allele. No occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied, so the TF choice and allelic direction are untested guesses.
If the site is a regulatory element, stronger TCF7L2 binding on the alt allele could increase its activity; the element itself has not been established.
The putative element would alter expression of an unknown local target gene; no variant-to-gene link is established.
The proposed effect would occur in HCT 116 cells if TCF7L2 occupies the site and the element is active there; neither condition is established.
A resulting change in target-gene expression could influence colorectal cancer risk, but the direction and gene are unknown.

predictions: The G allele will show greater TCF7L2-dependent activity than the T allele in HCT 116 cells.
Reducing TCF7L2 will diminish the allele-specific activity difference.
falsified_if: TCF7L2 does not occupy the site in HCT 116 cells, or the alleles show no TCF7L2-dependent activity difference in a suitable assay.

chains.title: Speculative HNF4A-dependent repression
chains.element: A putative cis-regulatory element overlapping rs13078086; its regulatory activity is unestablished.

links.claim: Hypothesis: the T (ref) allele binds HNF4A more strongly than the G (alt) allele. No occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied, so this direction is an untested guess.
If HNF4A represses an active local element, stronger binding on the ref allele could reduce its activity; repression at this site is not established.
The putative element would alter expression of an unknown local target gene; no target gene is identified.
The proposed effect would occur in HCT 116 cells if HNF4A occupies and regulates the site; this is unverified.
Loss of the proposed HNF4A-dependent repression on the alt allele could affect colorectal cancer risk, but the target and consequence are unknown.

predictions: The T allele will show greater HNF4A binding and lower local regulatory activity than the G allele.
Reducing HNF4A will weaken or eliminate that allele-specific activity difference.
falsified_if: HNF4A does not occupy the site, or the T allele does not show greater HNF4A-dependent repression than the G allele.

chains.title: Speculative JUN-dependent activation
chains.element: A putative cis-regulatory element overlapping rs13078086; its regulatory activity is unestablished.

links.claim: Hypothesis: the G (alt) allele binds JUN more strongly than the T (ref) allele. No occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result is supplied, so this is an untested candidate, not a supported binding call.
If JUN activates a regulatory element at this site, stronger binding on the alt allele could increase its activity; this regulatory role is unestablished.
The putative element would alter expression of an unknown local target gene; no target gene is established.
The proposed effect would occur in HCT 116 cells if JUN occupies and activates the site; this is unverified.
A resulting expression change could influence colorectal cancer risk, but neither the gene nor the direction of the disease effect is known.

predictions: The G allele will show greater JUN-dependent activity than the T allele in HCT 116 cells.
Reducing JUN will diminish the allele-specific activity difference.
falsified_if: JUN does not occupy the site, or the alleles show no JUN-dependent activity difference in a suitable assay.

matrix.test: Compare matched T- and G-allele sequence reporters in HCT 116 cells, with and without TCF7L2 depletion; assess reporter activity and whether the allelic difference depends on TCF7L2.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent activity difference, or any difference is not TCF7L2-dependent.
The G allele has greater activity than the T allele, and TCF7L2 depletion reduces the difference.
This TCF7L2-focused test does not support the proposed HNF4A-dependent repression; a separate HNF4A perturbation would be needed to test H2.
This TCF7L2-focused test does not support the proposed JUN-dependent activation; a separate JUN perturbation would be needed to test H3.

next_experiment: Run the matched-allele reporter assay in HCT 116 cells with and without TCF7L2 depletion. It is the most direct low-complexity test of the leading non-null chain against the null, although a reporter result alone would not establish the endogenous target gene or disease mechanism.
